title: Home Office Stipend Refresh for an Employee Grandfathered on the Old Cycle
scenario_text:
Pinehaven Retail revised its remote-work equipment stipend in mid-2024.

Version 1 (effective January 1, 2022) states: "Eligible remote employees receive a one-time home office stipend of $1,500, with refresh eligibility every 3 years from the last stipend date."

Version 2 (effective June 1, 2024) states: "Eligible remote employees receive a $1,000 stipend, with refresh eligibility every 4 years, subject to manager approval." v2 includes a transition clause: "Employees who received a stipend under v1 retain their v1 refresh cycle (3 years) for their next refresh only; the refresh amount and all subsequent cycles follow v2. Employees receiving their first stipend on or after June 1, 2024 are fully governed by v2."

The HRIS record for employee E-4410 shows: Last Stipend Date 2022-08-01, Last Stipend Amount $1,500 (issued under v1), Employment Status Active/Remote. It is currently July 2025.

An HR partner emails the benefits team on 2025-07-10: "E-4410 is asking about a home office equipment refresh. Their last stipend was issued August 2022 at $1,500 under the old policy. The stipend rules changed in mid-2024, so I want to get this right: when exactly are they next eligible for a refresh, and what dollar amount should we plan to issue given that the policy has since been revised?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the HRIS record, determine E-4410's next refresh date and amount.
question: When is E-4410 next eligible for a stipend refresh, and for how much?
choices: Eligible on August 1, 2025 (v1's 3-year cycle applies to the next refresh) for $1,000 (the v2 amount).
Eligible on August 1, 2025 for $1,500, because both the v1 refresh cycle and the v1 stipend amount carry forward to the next refresh.
Eligible on August 1, 2026 for $1,000, because v2's 4-year refresh cycle applies to the next refresh.
Not eligible on any fixed date; the next refresh is available only once a manager approves it under v2, with no set timing.
